definition_en: something accepted as true without proof, or the act of taking on a duty
core_image: 一块没有验过的地基被当作稳固
scene: 报告开头先列了三条前提。 The plan rests on the assumption that prices stay flat.
sceneCN: 这里 assumption 是「假定」（第 1 个义项：未经验证就被接受的前提）；句意是计划建立在物价不变这一假定上。

senses.title: Thing taken as true
senses.definition: something you accept as true without proof
senses.definitionCN: 未经证明就被当作成立的前提
senses.example: The plan rests on the assumption that prices stay flat.
senses.exampleCN: 计划建立在物价不变这一假定上。
senses.why: Assumption is assume plus -tion, turning the act of taking a claim up into the claim itself, the thing a plan leans on before proof arrives.
senses.whyCN: assumption 是 assume 加 -tion，把「拿过来接受」的动作变成被接受的那条内容，也就是计划在证据到来前所倚靠的前提。

senses.title: Act of taking on
senses.definition: the act of taking on power, duty or an office
senses.definitionCN: 接过权力、职责或职位的行为
senses.example: The assumption of office takes place in May.
senses.exampleCN: 就职仪式在五月举行。
senses.why: The old Latin sense of taking something onto oneself survives as a formal noun for entering an office or taking up a duty.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语「取到自己身上」的旧义保留下来，成为正式说法，指就任职位或承担职责。

intro.en: Assumption is the noun of taking up, whether a belief or an office.
intro.cn: assumption 是「拿起、接过」的名词，接过的可以是一种看法，也可以是一个职位。

items.en: sumere meant 'to take'.
items.cn: sumere 意为「拿」。

items.en: assumere meant 'to take to oneself'.
items.cn: assumere 意为「取到自己身上」。

items.en: assumptio meant 'a taking up'.
items.cn: assumptio 意为「拿起、接过」。

items.en: Old French assumer kept both the logical and official senses.
items.cn: 古法语 assumer 兼有逻辑与职务两方面的含义。

items.en: English assumption fixed the sense of an unproved premise.
items.cn: 英语把 assumption 固定为「未经证明的前提」。

note.en: The look-alike group is the sume family; the near-meaning group names premises and guesses.
note.cn: 形近组是 sume 词族；近义组是表示前提与推测的词。

normalIntro.en: An assumption is a floor nobody has tested before building on it.
normalIntro.cn: assumption 是一块没验过就被踩上去的地板。

normal.en: The phrase on the assumption that introduces the unproved point.
normal.cn: 短语 on the assumption that 引出那个未经验证的判断。

normal.en: In academic writing assumptions are usually stated and then tested.
normal.cn: 学术写作里通常先点明假设，再加以检验。

normal.en: The second sense is formal and appears with office or power.
normal.cn: 第二个义项较正式，常与职位或权力连用。

normal.en: The ending is -tion, so the noun refers to a thing or an act.
normal.cn: 结尾是 -tion，因此名词指事物或行为。

normal.en: Do not write an assumption of that for the everyday sense.
normal.cn: 日常「假定」义不用 an assumption of that 这种结构。

abstract.en: See a house built on a slab nobody checked.
abstract.cn: 想象房子盖在一块没人检查过的板上。

abstract.en: See a question mark drawn over a number in a report.
abstract.cn: 想象报告里的数字上被画了问号。

abstract.en: See a hand receiving a seal of office.
abstract.cn: 想象一双手接过任职印章。

examples.en: Her argument begins with a false assumption.
examples.cn: 她的论证从一个错误的假设开始。

dict_mnemonic.text: assume（假定、承担）加 -tion：被拿过来当作前提的那条内容是假设；把职位接过来这件事本身，是就任。

sensesIntro.cn: 未经证明就接受的看法，与在仪式上接过的职位，都是被「拿起」的东西。

intro.cn: 这个名词保留拉丁语「拿取」之义，-tion 标记结果。

definition_en: very unusual and impressive; much greater than usual; strange and surprising
core_image: 一朵普通花丛中突然开出的巨大奇异花朵
scene: 她展现出非凡的勇气。 She showed extraordinary courage.
sceneCN: 这里 extraordinary 是「非凡的、出色的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她展现出非凡的勇气。

senses.title: Far beyond usual
senses.definition: much greater or better than usual
senses.definitionCN: 远超过平常水平或质量的
senses.example: She showed extraordinary courage.
senses.exampleCN: 她展现出非凡的勇气。
senses.why: The core sense is standing outside the ordinary.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是站在平常之外。

senses.title: Very unusual
senses.definition: very unusual and not happening often
senses.definitionCN: 非常不寻常且不常发生的
senses.example: The team met under extraordinary circumstances.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在特殊情况下开会。
senses.why: Rare events stand outside normal rules.
senses.whyCN: 罕见事件站在常规之外。

senses.title: Strange and surprising
senses.definition: so strange that it surprises people
senses.definitionCN: 奇怪到令人惊讶的
senses.example: He told an extraordinary story about the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲了一个关于大海的离奇故事。
senses.why: The unusual becomes the astonishing.
senses.whyCN: 不寻常变成令人惊异。

intro.en: Extraordinary joins Latin extra, outside, and ordinarius, ordinary.
intro.cn: extraordinary 由拉丁语 extra（在外面）与 ordinarius（普通的）组合而成。

items.en: Extra means outside or beyond.
items.cn: extra 意为在外面或超出。

items.en: Ordinarius means ordinary or usual.
items.cn: ordinarius 意为普通的、通常的。

items.en: The pieces mean outside the ordinary.
items.cn: 两部分合起来意为「超出普通」。

items.en: The word passes through French into English.
items.cn: 这个词经法语进入英语。

items.en: Extraordinary covers greatness and strangeness.
items.cn: 现代英语中 extraordinary 涵盖卓越与离奇。

note.en: Extraordinary is beyond ordinary; ordinary is usual.
note.cn: extraordinary 是超出普通的，ordinary 则是平常的。

normalIntro.en: Extraordinary describes what stands far outside the ordinary.
normalIntro.cn: extraordinary 描述远远站在普通之外的事物。

normal.en: She has an extraordinary memory for names.
normal.cn: 她对名字有非凡的记忆力。

normal.en: The rescue was an extraordinary effort.

normal.en: They met under extraordinary circumstances.

normal.en: The painting is quite extraordinary.

normal.en: He told an extraordinary tale of survival.
normal.cn: 他讲了一个离奇的生存故事。

abstract.en: Picture one huge flower rising above a plain field.
abstract.cn: 想象一朵巨大的花从普通田野中升起。

abstract.en: Imagine a quiet town where something amazing happens.
abstract.cn: 想象一个安静小镇上发生了惊人的事。

abstract.en: Think of a person who does what no one thought possible.

sensesIntro.en: Extraordinary means far beyond usual, very unusual, or strange and surprising.
sensesIntro.cn: extraordinary 意为远超平常、非常不寻常，或离奇惊人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one huge flower above a plain field.
core.cn: 核心意象：普通田野上高出一切的一朵巨花。

branches.en: The base sense is greatness beyond the usual.

branches.en: Rare events stand outside normal rules.

branches.en: The unusual becomes astonishing.

branches.en: Special circumstances often produce strange stories.

latinIntro.en: Latin extra and ordinarius are the two source elements.

definition_zh: 港口；港市；端口；左舷；（把舵）转向左舷；波尔图葡萄酒
definition_en: a harbor where ships load and unload, an opening on a device for a cable, the left side of a ship, a fortified wine from Porto, or to turn a ship to the left
core_image: 码头边一排起重机，一艘货轮把船头缓缓靠向岸壁
scene: 黎明前的海湾里，灯塔还亮着，一艘货轮正慢慢靠上码头。 By dawn the cargo ship had entered the port and begun to unload.
sceneCN: 这里 port 是「港口」（第 1 个义项：船只装卸货物的港湾）；句意为天亮时货轮已经进港开始卸货。图中可辨识物件：海湾、灯塔、货轮、码头。

pos.zh: 港口；港市；端口；左舷；波尔图葡萄酒
把舵转向左舷；使船靠左

由 sea 与 port 复合，义为「海港；港市」
由拉丁 porta（门）加 -al 构成，义为「门户；入口」
由 port 加 -age 构成，义为「水陆之间的搬运；搬运费」

senses.title: A harbor where ships load and unload
senses.definition: a place on a coast or river where ships can tie up and where goods and passengers are loaded or unloaded
senses.definitionCN: 海岸或河边供船只停靠、装卸货物和上下旅客的地方
senses.example: The fishing boats return to port before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 渔船在暴风雨来临前回到港口。
senses.why: Latin portus named a sheltered place where a ship could lie safely; English borrowed it early, so the first sense is simply that stopping place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 portus 指船只能安全停靠的有遮蔽之处；英语借入得很早，所以第一个义项就是这个停靠点本身。

senses.title: A socket for a cable or device
senses.definition: an opening or socket on a computer or machine where a cable, plug or storage device is connected
senses.definitionCN: 计算机或机器上用来连接线缆、插头或存储设备的开口或插槽
senses.example: Plug the monitor into the port at the back of the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 把显示器插到机器背面的接口上。
senses.why: A port is also a gateway, a sense that came through Latin porta, a door; the socket is the narrow doorway through which signals enter and leave a machine.
senses.whyCN: port 也曾指「门户」，这一支经拉丁语 porta（门）而来；插槽就是信号进出机器的那道窄门。

senses.title: The left side of a ship
senses.definition: the left-hand side of a ship or aircraft when you are facing the front
senses.definitionCN: 面朝船头或机头时，船或飞机的左侧
senses.example: The lighthouse passed along the port side as the ship turned.
senses.exampleCN: 船转向时，灯塔从船的左舷掠过。
senses.why: One common explanation is that ships tied up with their loading side to the quay, so the harbor side became the name for the left; the derivation is still debated.
senses.whyCN: 一种常见解释是，船进港时把装卸的一侧靠向码头，于是「靠港的那一边」成了左舷的名字；这一来源仍有争论。

senses.title: A fortified wine from Porto
senses.definition: a sweet, strong red wine made in the Douro valley and shipped through the city of Porto
senses.definitionCN: 在杜罗河谷酿造、经波尔图城运出的甜型高度红葡萄酒
senses.example: They finished dinner with a glass of port and some cheese.
senses.exampleCN: 他们以一杯波尔图葡萄酒配奶酪结束了晚餐。
senses.why: The drink took its English name from Porto, the Portuguese city at the river mouth, so a place name shrank into a short everyday word.
senses.whyCN: 这种酒的英语名取自河口城市波尔图，于是一个地名缩成了日常使用的短词。

senses.title: To turn a ship to the left
senses.definition: to turn a ship or its helm towards the left side
senses.definitionCN: 把船或船舵转向左侧
senses.example: The captain ported the helm to avoid the drifting buoy.
senses.exampleCN: 船长把舵转向左舷，避开漂来的浮标。
senses.why: Once port names the left side, the verb applies that direction to steering: to port the helm is to send the bow that way.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 port 成为左舷的名称，动词就把这个方向用到操舵上：把舵转向左舷，就是让船头朝那边摆。

intro.en: The short word port joins three Latin threads: portus, a harbor, porta, a gate, and the wine named after the city of Porto.
intro.cn: 这个短词 port 汇合了三条拉丁线索：portus（港口）、porta（门），以及得名于波尔图城的葡萄酒。

items.en: Portus meant a harbor or haven, a sheltered place where a ship could lie safely; it is generally connected with an old root for passing through or crossing.
items.cn: portus 意为港口、避风处，是船只能安全停泊的有遮蔽之处；一般认为它与表示「穿过、越过」的古老词根有关。

items.en: Porta meant a gate or door, and it is the source of port in the sense of an opening, including the socket on a computer.
items.cn: porta 意为大门、出入口；表示「开口」的 port 就来自这里，电脑上的插口也属于这一支。

items.en: English borrowed port for a harbor from Latin, partly through Old French; by the Middle Ages it named both seaports and gateways.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁语借来表示港口的 port，其中一部分经古法语传入；到中世纪，它既指海港，也指出入口。

items.en: Port came to name the left side of a ship, usually explained by the side laid against the quay for loading; the explanation is not certain.
items.cn: port 开始指船的左舷，通常解释为进港装卸时靠向码头的那一侧；这一解释并不确定。

items.en: Porto in Portugal gave port wine its name, while computing made port a socket for cables and signals.
items.cn: 葡萄牙的波尔图给了波尔图葡萄酒这个名字，计算机则让 port 成为线缆与信号用的插口。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and relatives of the short form; the near-meaning group gathers words for sheltered water and places where ships tie up.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个短词构成的复合词与同族词；近义组收表示避风水域与船只停靠处的词。

entries.definition: A place where aircraft take off and land, built on port in the old sense of a stopping place.
entries.definitionCN: 由 air 与 port 复合，指飞机起降的机场；这里的 port 保留了「停靠地」的旧义。

entries.definition: A town or city with a harbor used by seagoing ships.
entries.definitionCN: 由 sea 与 port 复合，指拥有海港的城市。

entries.definition: A doorway or entrance, especially a large one; from Latin porta.
entries.definitionCN: 与表示「门」的 port 同出拉丁 porta，义为门户、入口。

entries.definition: Able to be carried; built on Latin portare, a different source from the harbor word.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写相近，但来自拉丁 portare（搬运），与「港口」的 port 不是同一个拉丁词。

entries.definition: A sheltered body of water where ships can stay safely.
entries.definitionCN: 港湾；强调有遮蔽、可避风，与港口近义。

entries.definition: A structure at the water's edge where a ship is loaded, repaired or kept.
entries.definitionCN: 码头；船坞；强调靠岸装卸或修船的具体设施。

entries.definition: A flat platform at a harbor where ships are loaded and unloaded.
entries.definitionCN: 码头；强调沿岸用于装卸的平台。

entries.definition: A small harbor designed for pleasure boats.
entries.definitionCN: 游艇码头；专供休闲船只停泊的小港。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on Latin portus for a harbor, and the same spelling has picked up a gate, a ship's side and a wine along the way.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词立足于表示港口的拉丁语 portus，同一个拼写沿途又接上了门、船舷与一种酒。

normal.en: Port comes from Latin portus, a harbor, and English had the word early enough to use it for any place a ship stops.
normal.cn: port 来自拉丁语 portus（港口），英语借入很早，凡船停靠之处都能用它。

normal.en: A computer port is a gate for signals, which is why this sense goes back to Latin porta, a door, rather than to portus.
normal.cn: 电脑端口是信号进出的门，所以这一义项上溯的是拉丁语 porta（门），而不是 portus。

normal.en: Port side is the left side of a ship; the usual explanation is that the loading side lay against the quay in harbor.
normal.cn: port side 是船的左舷；常见解释是装卸的一侧在港里靠着码头。

normal.en: Port wine is named after Porto, the Portuguese city at the mouth of the Douro.
normal.cn: port wine 得名于杜罗河口的葡萄牙城市波尔图。

normal.en: Airport and seaport stretch port from a harbor to any place where vehicles stop and load.
normal.cn: airport 与 seaport 把 port 从港湾扩展到任何车辆停靠、装卸的地方。

abstract.en: A harbor is where a journey pauses, so one short word can name a ship's rest, a signal's doorway and a glass at the end of dinner.
abstract.cn: 港口是旅程暂停的地方，所以一个短词既能指船的歇脚处，也能指信号的门口和晚餐末尾的一杯酒。

abstract.en: A port is a controlled opening: water, people and data all pass through a narrow gate that can be watched.
abstract.cn: 端口是一道受控的开口：水、人和数据都得从一道可以被看守的窄门通过。

abstract.en: The left side of a ship is named from the shore it once faced, a reminder that directions are often borrowed from land.
abstract.cn: 船的左舷用它曾经面对的岸来命名，这提醒人：方向常常是从陆地借来的。

examples.en: By dawn the cargo ship had entered the port and begun to unload.
examples.cn: 天亮时货轮已经进港开始卸货。

examples.en: Plug the monitor into the port at the back of the machine.
examples.cn: 把显示器插到机器背面的接口上。

examples.en: They finished dinner with a glass of port and some cheese.
examples.cn: 他们以一杯波尔图葡萄酒配奶酪结束了晚餐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「波特」——船停在港湾里卸货，杯里也盛着波尔图来的甜酒；port 就是港口，也是端口、左舷与波尔图酒。

root: port 背后有三条拉丁线：portus（港口、避风处）、porta（门，电脑端口由此而来）与 portare（搬运，portable、porter 由此而来）；三者深层同源，但在拉丁语里是彼此不同的词。port wine 则得名于葡萄牙城市波尔图。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a sheltered place where movement stops; the senses branch into the harbor, the gate for signals, the ship's left side, the wine of Porto and the act of turning that way.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是运动暂停的有遮蔽之处；义项由此分出港口、信号的门、船左舷、波尔图酒，以及朝那边转舵的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cranes along a quay, a freighter easing its bow towards the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：码头边一排起重机，一艘货轮把船头缓缓靠向岸壁。

branches.en: cranes lifting containers beside a docked freighter
branches.cn: 起重机在靠岸的货轮旁吊起集装箱

branches.en: a cable clicking into a socket at the back of a machine

latinIntro.en: Three Latin words stand behind this short form: portus for a harbor, porta for a gate, and portare for carrying; they are related at a deeper level but were separate words in Latin.

items.meaning: sea plus port, a harbor town
items.meaningCN: 由 sea 与 port 复合，指海港城市

definition_en: an animal doctor, or a person who has served in the armed forces; as a verb, to check someone or something carefully before acceptance
core_image: 给动物看病的人：一件白大褂，面前站着一只不安的小狗
scene: 宠物诊所里，主人轻轻按住小猫的爪子。 The vet examined the injured paw carefully before giving the vaccine.
sceneCN: 这里 vet 是「兽医」（第 1 个义项：给动物治病的医生）；句意是兽医在打疫苗前仔细检查受伤的爪子。

pos.zh: 审查；检查（人或物）是否合格

collocations.phrase: take the dog to the vet

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 veteranus（老兵）演变而来，本词 vet 是其口语缩略；义为「老兵；经验丰富的人」
veteran 同族形容词，义为「兽医的；动物医疗的」

senses.title: An animal doctor
senses.definition: a person trained to give medical care to sick or injured animals
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、给生病或受伤动物提供医疗照护的人
senses.example: The vet gave the puppy a check-up.
senses.exampleCN: 兽医给小狗做了一次体检。
senses.why: The word is short for veterinary surgeon, the professional who treats animals instead of people.
senses.whyCN: 本词是 veterinary surgeon（兽医外科医生）的口语缩略，指给动物而非人类治病的职业者，核心画面就是白大褂加小动物。

senses.title: A former soldier
senses.definition: a person who has served for a long time or in a war, especially in the armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 长期服役或经历过战争的人，尤指退伍军人
senses.example: The old vet marched at the head of the parade.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老兵走在游行队伍的最前面。
senses.why: It is the colloquial shortening of veteran, from Latin veteranus meaning one who has grown old in service.
senses.whyCN: 它是 veteran 的口语缩略；拉丁语 veteranus 指「在服役中变老的人」，所以引申为身经百战的老兵。

senses.title: An experienced person in a field
senses.definition: someone with long experience in a particular field or organization
senses.definitionCN: 在某一领域或组织中经验丰富的人
senses.example: She is a vet of the film industry, having produced movies for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 她是电影界的老手，制作电影已有三十年。
senses.why: Long service in the army extends metaphorically to long service anywhere, so the old hand and the old soldier share one word.
senses.whyCN: 军中的长期服役被隐喻推广到任何领域的长期资历，于是「老资格的人」与「老兵」共用同一个词。

senses.title: To check carefully before acceptance
senses.definition: to examine someone or something carefully to make sure they are suitable or safe
senses.definitionCN: 仔细审查某人或某物，确认其合适或安全
senses.example: Every employee is vetted before joining the team.
senses.exampleCN: 每位员工入职前都要经过审查。
senses.why: A doctor examines an animal thoroughly before treating it; that thorough inspection was extended to scrutinizing people and documents.
senses.whyCN: 兽医接诊前要先对动物做彻底检查，这种彻底查验被引申为对人员、文件的严格甄别审查。

senses.title: To treat an animal as a vet
senses.definition: to work as a vet, giving medical treatment to animals
senses.definitionCN: 以兽医身份工作，为动物进行治疗
senses.example: He has vetted farm animals in this village for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在这座村子给家畜看病已有二十年。
senses.why: The profession name naturally turns into a verb for doing the profession's work, just like nurse or coach.
senses.whyCN: 职业名词自然转为动词表示从事该职业的工作，正如 nurse（护理）、coach（执教）一样。

intro.en: Vet is a double shortening: veterinary surgeon for the animal doctor, and veteran for the old soldier.
intro.cn: vet 是双重缩略：作为「兽医」是 veterinary surgeon 的缩略；作为「老兵」是 veteran 的缩略。

items.en: veteranus meant 'aged, one who has served long', from vetus, 'old'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 veteranus 意为「年长的、长期服役的」，词根 vetus 意为「老」。

items.en: veterinarius described things relating to beasts of burden, the root of veterinary.
items.cn: 拉丁语 veterinarius 描述与驮兽相关的事物，是 veterinary 的来源。

items.en: Veteran entered English for old soldiers; veterinary surgeon named the animal doctor.
items.cn: veteran 于十七至十九世纪进入英语，指老兵；veterinary surgeon 指动物医生。

items.en: Both long titles were clipped to vet in everyday speech.
items.cn: 在日常口语中，两个冗长的头衔都被缩短成 vet。

items.en: The noun vet was turned into a verb meaning to scrutinize before acceptance.
items.cn: 名词 vet 又转为动词，表示「录用前的审查甄别」。

note.en: Watch the clipped forms: vet comes from two long words, and neighbors like veto only look alike.
note.cn: 注意缩略形式：vet 来自两个长词，而 veto（否决）等邻居只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: an official power to reject a decision or proposal
entries.definitionCN: 否决权；否决。只是拼写相近，词源不同（拉丁语 vetare，禁止）。

entries.definition: a person with long experience, especially a former soldier
entries.definitionCN: 老兵；经验丰富者。vet 作「老兵」解时正是它的口语缩略。

entries.definition: relating to the medical care of animals
entries.definitionCN: 兽医的；动物医疗的。vet 作「兽医」解时源自其首音节。

entries.definition: a doctor who treats human patients
entries.definitionCN: 医生；内科医生。对象是人类，与兽医保卫的对象相对。

entries.definition: a person who tests or inspects others formally
entries.definitionCN: 审查者；检查者。与 vet 动词义的「甄别审查」相近，但更正式。

entries.definition: to examine something very carefully
entries.definitionCN: 仔细审查。与 vet 的动词义几乎重合，但不含「录用前把关」的语感。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks built from the word's real history and uses.
normalIntro.cn: 基于词源与真实用法的五条联想。

normal.en: Vet clips veterinary surgeon: the vet vets your pet.
normal.cn: vet 是 veterinary surgeon 的缩略：兽医给宠物看病（vet your pet）。

normal.en: Vet also clips veteran: the war vet sits beside the dog vet.
normal.cn: vet 也是 veteran 的缩略：老兵与兽医共用一个短词。

normal.en: To vet a candidate is to give him a full check-up, like an animal at the clinic.
normal.cn: 审查候选人类似兽医接诊：先做全面「体检」再放行。

normal.en: Latin vetus means old; veterans are those grown old in service.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 vetus 意为「老」，老兵就是服役到老的人。

normal.en: Verb forms double the T: vet, vetted, vetting.
normal.cn: 动词变化双写 T：vet, vetted, vetting。

abstract.en: Picture a white coat with one pocket for pills and another for medals.
abstract.cn: 想象一件白大褂，一个口袋装药片，另一个装勋章。

abstract.en: Imagine a small dog waiting quietly under the clinic lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象诊灯下安静等待的小狗。

abstract.en: Feel a gatekeeper's stamp: checked, approved, allowed through.
abstract.cn: 感受把关者的印章：查毕、合格、放行。

examples.en: We took the sick cat to the vet this morning.
examples.cn: 今天早上我们带生病的猫去看兽医。

examples.en: His grandfather was a navy vet who loved telling stories.
examples.cn: 他的祖父是位海军老兵，爱讲故事。

examples.en: All news reports are vetted before publication.
examples.cn: 所有新闻报道发表前都要经过审查。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂它」——兽医的工作就是喂它、护理它；老兵回营也是为了有口饭「喂它」。

root: vet 作名词有两条来源：一是 veterinary（拉丁语 veterinarius「与驮兽有关的」）的缩略，指兽医；二是 veteran（拉丁语 veteranus，词根 vetus「老」）的缩略，指老兵。动词义由「彻底检查」引申而来。

sensesIntro.en: From the animal doctor and the old soldier, the word stretches to experienced hands and then to the act of scrutiny.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「兽医」「老兵」两个名词核心，延伸出「老手」的比喻义，再引申出动词「审查」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a short white coat that serves animals, soldiers, and the checkpoint
core.cn: 核心意象：一件服务动物、军人，并守在检查关卡前的白大褂

branches.en: The clinic work
branches.cn: 诊所里的诊疗工作，从名词职业到动词行医。

branches.en: The battle-tested soldier
branches.cn: 身经百战的退伍军人。

branches.en: The veteran of any trade
branches.cn: 任何行业的资深老手。

branches.en: The thorough check before trust
branches.cn: 信任之前的彻底核查。

branches.en: From inspection to clearance
branches.cn: 从检查到放行，把关的完整闭环。

intro.en: The family of vet- rests on Latin vetus, old, and branches into medicine, war, and checking.
intro.cn: vet- 词族建立在拉丁语 vetus（老）之上，分支延伸到医疗、战争与审查领域。

latinIntro.en: Latin relatives that share the root of growing old in service.
latinIntro.cn: 共享「服役至老」这一词根的拉丁同源词。

definition_en: to pause before acting because of doubt, or to be unwilling
core_image: 脚已经抬起，却在门前停住
scene: 她在门口犹豫了一会儿才敲门。 She hesitated at the door before knocking.
sceneCN: 这里 hesitate 是「犹豫」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她在门口犹豫了一会儿才敲门。

senses.title: Pause in doubt
senses.definition: to pause before doing something because you are not sure
senses.definitionCN: 因不确定而在行动前停顿
senses.example: She hesitated at the door before knocking.
senses.exampleCN: 她在门口犹豫了一会儿才敲门。
senses.why: This is the core sense of doubt.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示疑虑的核心义项。

senses.title: Be unwilling
senses.definition: to be unwilling to do something
senses.definitionCN: 不愿意做某事
senses.example: He hesitated to tell them the truth.
senses.exampleCN: 他不愿把真相告诉他们。
senses.why: Reluctance also makes a person pause.
senses.whyCN: 不情愿也会让人停顿。

intro.en: Hesitate comes from a Latin verb meaning to stick fast.
intro.cn: hesitate 来自拉丁语动词，意为黏住、卡住。

items.en: Haesitare meant to stick or hesitate.
items.cn: haesitare 意为黏住或迟疑。

items.en: Haesitatus was its past participle.
items.cn: haesitatus 是它的过去分词。

items.cn: hesitate 作为表示疑虑的动词进入英语。

items.en: The phrase do not hesitate became polite.
items.cn: do not hesitate 成为礼貌用语。

items.en: Hesitate widened to mean be unwilling.

note.en: Hesitate is compared with look-alike words and with words for pausing.

normalIntro.en: To hesitate is to stand still inside a decision.
normalIntro.cn: hesitate 就是在一个决定里站着不动。

normal.cn: 她在门口犹豫了一会儿才敲门。

normal.en: He hesitated to tell them the truth.
normal.cn: 他不愿把真相告诉他们。

normal.en: Do not hesitate to ask for help.

normal.en: He answered without hesitating.

abstract.en: To hesitate is to hear two roads at once.

abstract.en: The moment of hesitation is often the whole decision.
abstract.cn: 犹豫的那一刻，常常就是整个决定。

abstract.en: Those who never hesitate rarely change their minds.

sensesIntro.en: Hesitate means to pause from doubt, or to be unwilling to act.

core.en: A step that stops halfway to the ground.

latinIntro.en: The Latin base haesit- meant to stick fast.

definition_en: the facts and conditions that affect an event, the conditions of a person's life, or a person's financial position
core_image: 一个人站在四周密密麻麻的条件中间
scene: 雨下得很大，末班车又提前开走了。 Under the circumstances, we decided to stay.
sceneCN: 这里 circumstances 指「情况」（第 1 个义项：影响某个决定的周边事实）；句意是在这种情况下，我们决定留下。

senses.title: The facts around an event
senses.definition: the facts and conditions that affect an event or a decision
senses.definitionCN: 影响某个事件或决定的周边事实与条件
senses.example: Under the circumstances, we decided to stay.
senses.exampleCN: 在这种情况下，我们决定留下。
senses.why: Latin circumstantia meant standing around, so the facts standing around an event took the name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 circumstantia 意为站在四周，围绕事件的事实便得了这个名字。

senses.title: Surrounding conditions
senses.definition: the conditions of life that surround a person or a group
senses.definitionCN: 围绕一个人或一群人的生活条件
senses.example: Children here grow up in difficult circumstances.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的孩子在艰难的环境中长大。
senses.why: What stands around a person forms the setting of a whole life.
senses.whyCN: 围绕一个人站立的东西，构成了整段生活的背景。

senses.title: Financial position
senses.definition: the level of money and comfort of a person or a family
senses.definitionCN: 个人或家庭的金钱与生活水平
senses.example: Her circumstances improved after the new job.
senses.exampleCN: 新工作之后她的境况好转了。
senses.why: Money became the measure of the ground a person stands on.
senses.whyCN: 金钱成了衡量一个人脚下立足之地的尺度。

intro.en: Circumstance is Latin for a standing around, as conditions stand around an event.
intro.cn: circumstance 在拉丁语中意为「站在四周」，正如条件围绕事件而立。

items.en: Circum meant around on every side.
items.cn: circum 意为四周环绕。

items.en: Stare meant to stand.
items.cn: stare 意为站立。

items.en: Circumstantia named the things standing around.
items.cn: circumstantia 指站在四周的事物。

items.en: Circonstance carried the word into French.
items.cn: circonstance 把这个词带进法语。

items.en: English circumstance named the setting of an act.
items.cn: 英语 circumstance 指一个行为的背景。

items.en: The plural widened to life conditions and money.
items.cn: 复数形式扩展到生活条件与金钱状况。

note.cn: 形近组共享 circum- 开头，近义组列出背景与条件。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the standing-around image, the three senses and the fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「站在四周」的意象、三层意思以及固定搭配。

normal.en: Split circumstance into circum and stance: everything standing around you.
normal.cn: 把 circumstance 拆成 circum 与 stance：站在你四周的一切。

normal.en: Under the circumstances is the most common frame, meaning because of the facts.
normal.cn: under the circumstances 是最常见的框架，意为「鉴于这些事实」。

normal.en: Under no circumstances is a strong refusal, and it keeps the same plural shape.
normal.cn: under no circumstances 表示坚决否定，形状仍是复数。

normal.en: Circumstantial evidence is evidence from the things standing around a case.

abstract.en: Picture a person standing still while rain, traffic and clock hands press in.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站住不动，雨、车流与钟表的指针都压过来。

abstract.en: Picture a small family in a narrow room with one lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小家庭挤在有盏灯的窄房间里。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of bills on a kitchen table.
abstract.cn: 想象厨房桌上放着一叠账单。

examples.en: Under the circumstances, the delay was understandable.
examples.cn: 在这种情况下，延误是可以理解的。

examples.en: Many families live in hard circumstances.

examples.en: He rose above his circumstances through study.
examples.cn: 他靠学习摆脱了自己的境况。

sensesIntro.en: Things standing around an act give the case facts, then the setting of a life, and finally the money a person stands on.
sensesIntro.cn: 围绕行为而立的事物先给出具体情况，再给出生活背景，最后给出一个人脚下的钱财。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure standing in the middle of pressing conditions.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在层层条件包围的中间。

branches.en: The facts of a case are the first sense.
branches.cn: 案件的具体事实是第一层意思。

branches.en: The setting of a life is the plural at work.
branches.cn: 生活背景是复数形式的常见用法。

branches.en: Money is the narrowest and most personal sense.
branches.cn: 金钱是最窄也最贴近个人的义项。

branches.en: One event and a whole life both sit inside conditions.
branches.cn: 单个事件与整段人生都坐在条件之中。

branches.en: Money decides much of the ground a family stands on.
branches.cn: 金钱决定了一个家庭脚下的大部分立足之地。

intro.en: The stem builds a plural, an adjective and an adverb from one Latin frame.
intro.cn: 这个词干在一个拉丁框架上构成复数、形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin circum around plus stare to stand produced circumstantia, the base of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 circum（周围）加 stare（站立）构成 circumstantia，是整个词族的词基。

items.exampleCN: 当时的情况对我们不利。

items.example: The case rested on circumstantial proof.

items.exampleCN: 这一关联是以间接方式证明的。
circum- 是 circumstance 的开头。

items.example: Stance carries the sense of standing.

latinEntries.example: Circumstantia is the direct source of circumstance.
latinEntries.exampleCN: circumstantia 是 circumstance 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Circumstare joins around with to stand.
latinEntries.exampleCN: circumstare 把周围与站立合在一起。

definition_zh: 统计数值；统计数据；（statistics）统计学；统计资料
definition_en: a single number giving measured information, or statistics, the science of collecting and studying such numbers
core_image: 一张布满格子的表格，每个格子里坐着一个被数出来的数字
scene: 人口普查的办公室里，调查员整理成摞问卷。 Each statistic in the census report came from thousands of questionnaires.
sceneCN: 这里 statistic 是「统计数值」（第 1 个义项：由数据算出的一个数字）；句意为普查报告中的每个统计数字都来自数千份问卷。

pos.zh: 名词：统计数值；统计数字

collocations.zh: 能说明问题的统计数字

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「统计的；统计学的」
由本词加指人后缀构成，义为「统计学家；统计员」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「统计上；按统计来看」

senses.title: A single number giving measured information
senses.definition: one number that represents a fact measured or counted from data
senses.definitionCN: 由数据测量或计数得出的、代表某一事实的一个数字
senses.example: One sad statistic is that most new cafés close within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 一个令人遗憾的统计数字是，多数新咖啡馆在一年内关门。
senses.why: One cell of the big table holds one counted number.
senses.whyCN: 大表格里的一个格子装着一个被数出来的数字。

senses.title: Statistics, the science of collecting and studying numbers
senses.definition: the study of collecting, organizing, and interpreting numerical data, usually as the plural subject statistics
senses.definitionCN: 收集、整理和解释数字数据的学科，通常以复数形式 statistics 指这门学科
senses.example: She is studying statistics at university.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学里学习统计学。
senses.why: The whole table, not one cell, becomes the field of study itself.
senses.whyCN: 当整张表格而不是单个格子成为研究对象，就成了一门学科。

senses.title: Statistics, a set of numerical facts collected together
senses.definition: a collection of numerical facts about a subject, such as population or prices
senses.definitionCN: 关于某一主题（如人口或物价）汇总起来的成套数字事实
senses.example: Tourism statistics for the year were published in March.
senses.exampleCN: 该年度的旅游统计资料于三月发布。
senses.why: Many filled cells laid side by side form a body of facts.
senses.whyCN: 许多填好的格子并排排列，汇成一套事实资料。

intro.en: Statistic grew from the idea of the state's science: numbers first collected for governments to govern by.
intro.cn: statistic 源于「国家的科学」：数字最初是为政府治国而收集的。

items.en: Statisticum collegium, a 17th-century term, meant a council concerned with state affairs.
items.cn: 17 世纪新拉丁语 statisticum collegium 指研究国事的学问团体。

items.en: Statista meant a person skilled in statecraft, dealing with facts of the state.
items.cn: 意大利语 statista 指精通国政之人，处理与国家有关的事实。

items.en: Statistik, coined in the 18th century, meant the analysis of state data such as population and land.
items.cn: 18 世纪德语 Statistik 指对国家数据（人口、土地等）的分析。

items.en: Statistics entered English first as state data, then widened to any numerical science of data.
items.cn: statistics 进入英语时先指国家数据，后扩展为泛指的数据科学。

items.en: The singular statistic settled for one number, while statistics names both the science and collected data.
items.cn: 单数 statistic 定型为「一个统计数值」，statistics 兼指学科与统计资料。

note.en: Statistic shares its state-root with state and status, and sits near words of different roots for measured facts.
note.cn: statistic 与 state、status 同含「国家」词根，义场又靠近词源不同的若干「数据事实」词。

entries.definition: a political country, a condition, or to say something formally
entries.definitionCN: 国家；状态；陈述；与 statistic 同含「国家」词根

entries.definition: the social or professional position of someone
entries.definitionCN: 地位；身份；同根词，源自「站立、立国」意象

entries.definition: a place where trains stop, or where someone is posted
entries.definitionCN: 车站；驻地；同根词，原义「立定之处」

entries.definition: a number, especially one shown in official records
entries.definitionCN: 数字；数额，泛指数字本身，不强调统计方法

entries.definition: facts or information used for calculating or analyzing
entries.definitionCN: 数据；资料，是统计前的原始材料

entries.definition: an official count of a population
entries.definitionCN: 人口普查，是产生统计数值的典型来源

entries.definition: a standard of measurement used for judging performance
entries.definitionCN: 指标；度量标准，强调用于衡量的规则

normalIntro.en: Anchor the word to its state-root family and the real subject name statistics.
normalIntro.cn: 把单词锚定在「国家」词根家族和学科名 statistics 上。

normal.en: The root stat- means state: numbers first collected for governments.
normal.cn: 词根 stat- 意为「国家」：数字最早为政府而收集。

normal.en: Statistics is the school subject name, always plural.
normal.cn: statistics 是学科名称，始终用复数形式。

normal.en: State, status, station, and statistic all carry the same stat- root.
normal.cn: state、status、station、statistic 都带同一 stat- 词根。

normal.en: A statistician is the person who works with statistics.
normal.cn: statistician 是与统计打交道的人，即统计学家。

normal.en: Statistically significant is a fixed phrase in research writing.
normal.cn: statistically significant（统计上显著）是研究写作的固定说法。

abstract.en: Picture one glowing cell in a giant spreadsheet, holding a hard-won number.
abstract.cn: 想象巨型表格中一个发光的格子，装着一个来之不易的数字。

abstract.en: See a clerk long ago counting people for the king, the first statistic.
abstract.cn: 想象古代书吏为国王清点人口，那是最早的统计数字。

abstract.en: Feel the whole table turn into a classroom subject called statistics.
abstract.cn: 体会整张表格变成一门叫统计学的课堂科目。

examples.en: The jobless rate is a statistic that changes every month.
examples.cn: 失业率是每月都在变化的统计数字。

examples.en: Behind every statistic is a family with a story.
examples.cn: 每个统计数字背后都有一个有故事的家庭。

examples.en: Statistics can mislead when the sample is too small.
examples.cn: 样本太小时，统计结果可能造成误导。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯的提斯蒂克」——谐音「死记的题是提分的题」：把一堆数字死记住、统计好就能提分。

root: 源自拉丁语 status（国家；所立之姿），经意大利语 statista 与德语 Statistik 进入英语；与 state、station、status 同根，核心意象是「为立国而收集的数字」。

sensesIntro.en: From one counted cell of state data, the idea grows into the whole science of numbers and the collected body of facts.
sensesIntro.cn: 从国家数据表格中的一个格子，展开为整门数字科学以及汇总成套的统计资料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one counted number sitting in a cell of the state's great table
core.cn: 核心意象：国家大表格的格子里坐着一个被数出来的数字

branches.en: a single number measured from data
branches.cn: 由数据得出的单个数字

branches.en: the science of numbers as a subject
branches.cn: 作为学科的数字科学

branches.en: a collected set of numerical facts
branches.cn: 汇总成套的数字事实

branches.en: cells filled and laid side by side
branches.cn: 格子被填满并排成套

branches.en: the whole table taught in a classroom
branches.cn: 整张表格走进课堂成为学科

intro.en: The stat- family shows how a root for the state grew numbers, positions, and standing figures.
intro.cn: stat- 词族展示「国家」词根如何派生出数字、地位与立定之物。

latinIntro.en: From Latin status, the state and manner of standing, several English words descend.
latinIntro.cn: 多个英语词源自拉丁语 status（国家；所立之姿）。

items.meaning: the science or the collected data

items.structure: same root via Old French estat

items.meaning: relating to a practice or system
items.meaningCN: 形容词后缀，表与某体系相关

items.meaning: makes nouns for a person skilled in something

由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「统计上」

definition_zh: 电的；与电有关的；电气的；用电的
definition_en: relating to electricity as a system, to electrical engineering, or to equipment that runs on electricity
core_image: 配电箱盖一打开，一排排彩色线束和标签露出来
scene: 电工掀开墙上的盖板，露出一排烧焦的线头。 An electrical fault had started the fire.
sceneCN: 这里 electrical 是「与电有关的、电气的」（第 1 个义项：指电力系统与线路，而非单个电器）；句意是线路中一处电气故障引发了火灾。

pos.zh: 形容词：电的；与电有关的；电气的；用电的

forms.label: 比较级（形容词，多音节用 more）
最高级（形容词，多音节用 most）

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉 -al 得到，义为「电的；用电的」
由 electric 加 -ity 构成，义为「电；电力」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「用电力地；在电气方面」
由 electric 加 -ian 构成，义为「电工」

senses.title: Relating to electrical systems
senses.definition: relating to electricity as a system of supply, wiring and engineering
senses.definitionCN: 指作为供电、布线与工程系统的电
senses.example: She studied electrical engineering at college.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学学的是电气工程。
senses.why: The -al ending turns the noun electricity into a word about the field as a whole, so it suits systems rather than single devices.
senses.whyCN: -al 词尾把名词 electricity 变成指整个领域的词，因此它适合系统而不适合单个器具。

senses.title: Running on electricity
senses.definition: of equipment or appliances, operated by electricity, used as a general classifying word
senses.definitionCN: 指设备或器具由电力驱动，用作一般分类的说法
senses.example: Old electrical appliances use far more power.
senses.exampleCN: 旧家用电器耗电多得多。
senses.why: A whole class of goods is sorted by what drives them, so the classifying adjective takes the -al form.
senses.whyCN: 一整类商品按驱动方式分类，于是这个分类形容词采用了 -al 形式。

senses.title: Of the theory of electricity
senses.definition: relating to the scientific study of electricity and its properties
senses.definitionCN: 指对电及其性质的科学理论研究
senses.example: The paper compares the electrical properties of the two metals.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文比较了两种金属的电学性质。
senses.why: Properties belong to the science rather than to a machine, so the academic sense also takes -al.
senses.whyCN: 性质属于科学而不属于某台机器，所以学术义也用 -al 形式。

intro.en: Electrical is electric plus the Latin adjective ending -al; the stem goes back through Latin electrum to Greek elektron, amber.
intro.cn: electrical 是 electric 加拉丁语形容词词尾 -al；词干经拉丁语 electrum 上溯到希腊语 elektron（琥珀）。

items.en: Elektron meant amber, the substance that first showed the effect.
items.cn: elektron 意为「琥珀」，是最先显现这种效应的物质。

items.en: Seventeenth-century science coined electricus for the force amber shows.
items.cn: 十七世纪科学造出 electricus，指琥珀所显现的那股力。

items.en: English took the adjective and used it for bodies that attract and repel.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词，用于相互吸引与排斥的物体。

items.en: The -al form was added to speak of the whole field rather than one object.
items.cn: 加上 -al 的形式用来谈整个领域，而不是单个物体。

items.en: Engineering, wiring and appliances settled into the -al branch, leaving electric for the vivid and the specific.
items.cn: 工程、布线与家电固定在 -al 这一支，把 electric 留给更具体、更生动的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the electricity family; the near-meaning group separates electric, electronic and powered.
note.cn: 形近组收 electricity 词族；近义组区分 electric、electronic 与 powered。

entries.definition: Of electricity itself, or of one device that runs on it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电的；用电的」，多指力量本身或单个器具。

entries.definition: The energy of moving charges, or its supply to homes.
By means of electricity, or in electrical terms.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「用电力地；在电气方面」。

entries.definition: A tradesperson who fits and repairs wiring.
Working through circuits that control electrons, as phones and computers do.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电子的」，靠控制电子的电路工作，如手机与电脑。

entries.definition: Driven by a named source, such as solar-powered.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「以……为动力的」，须说明来源。

entries.definition: The public supply of electricity to a building.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「市电、供电网」，是 electrical 系统的来源。

normalIntro.en: These hooks open a fuse box, then draw the line between a single device and the whole system behind it.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子打开一个配电箱，再划清「单个器具」与「背后整套系统」的界线。

normal.en: The -al makes it about the field: electrical engineering, electrical fault.
normal.cn: -al 让它指向整个领域：电气工程、电气故障。

normal.en: An electric kettle is one object; electrical wiring is the system feeding it.
normal.cn: electric kettle 是一件东西；electrical wiring 是给它供电的系统。

normal.en: Electrical appliances as a class, not one appliance in the hand.
normal.cn: electrical appliances 指一整类，而不是手里那一件。

normal.en: Electrical properties belong to the science, not to the plug.
normal.cn: electrical properties 属于科学，而不属于插头。

normal.en: Electric can thrill; electrical stays technical.
normal.cn: electric 可以令人激动；electrical 始终偏技术。

abstract.en: Picture the inside of a fuse box, rows of coloured wires and labels.
abstract.cn: 想象配电箱内部，一排排彩色导线与标签。

abstract.en: The same current that lights a lamp also has a name as a system.
abstract.cn: 点亮灯泡的那股电流，作为系统另有一个名称。

abstract.en: Electrical is the map; electric is the spark on it.
abstract.cn: electrical 是地图；electric 是地图上那颗火花。

examples.en: She studied electrical engineering at college.
examples.cn: 她在大学学的是电气工程。

examples.en: Old electrical appliances use far more power.
examples.cn: 旧家用电器耗电多得多。

examples.en: The paper compares the electrical properties of the two metals.
examples.cn: 这篇论文比较了两种金属的电学性质。

root: 由 electric 加拉丁语形容词词尾 -al 构成；electric 源自希腊语 elektron「琥珀」，经拉丁语 electrum 与近代拉丁语 electricus 而来。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of electrical: the supply system, equipment classified by its power source, and the science of electricity.
sensesIntro.cn: electrical 的三个义项：供电与线路系统、按动力分类的电器，以及电学理论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open fuse box with rows of coloured wires and labels.
core.cn: 核心意象：打开的配电箱，成排彩色导线与标签。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: supply, wiring and the engineering that runs them.
branches.cn: 系统线：供电、布线以及管理它们的工程。

branches.en: THE CLASS: appliances sorted by what drives them.
branches.cn: 分类线：按驱动方式归类的一整批电器。

branches.en: THE SCIENCE: properties studied rather than used.
branches.cn: 科学线：被研究而非被使用的性质。

branches.en: THE SUPPLY: the system and the goods it feeds form one grid.
branches.cn: 供给线：系统与它供养的电器构成一张电网。

branches.en: THE THEORY: every fault is a lesson in the science.
branches.cn: 理论线：每一次故障都是科学的一课。

intro.en: Electrical is electric plus the Latin adjective -al; the whole branch stays close to the Greek word for amber.
intro.cn: electrical 是 electric 加拉丁语形容词词尾 -al；整支词都与希腊语「琥珀」保持很近的距离。

latinIntro.en: Greek elektron and Latin electrum are recorded; electricus and the -al form are later scientific constructions.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 elektron 与拉丁语 electrum 有记录；electricus 与加 -al 的形式则是后来的科学构造。

items.example: It carried the word into Latin.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个词带入拉丁语。

items.example: It was coined in the seventeenth century.

definition_en: a unit of heredity that passes features from parents to young, or a basic factor that decides a quality
core_image: 显微镜下细胞核里盘绕的遗传物质
scene: 每个基因都携带一条信息。 Each gene carries a message.
sceneCN: 这里 gene 是「基因」（第 1 个义项）；句意：每个基因都携带一条信息。

senses.title: Unit of heredity
senses.definition: a part of a cell that carries information from parents to their young
senses.definitionCN: 细胞中把信息从父母传给后代的组成部分
senses.example: Each gene carries a message.
senses.exampleCN: 每个基因都携带一条信息。
senses.why: This is the biological sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词的生物学义项。

senses.title: Deciding factor
senses.definition: a basic factor that is said to decide a quality or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 被认为决定某种特征或行为的基本因素
senses.example: The team has a gene for hard work.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍有一种勤奋的内在因素。
senses.why: Biology supplies a metaphor for built-in traits.
senses.whyCN: 生物学为与生俱来的特征提供了比喻。

intro.en: Gene was coined from a Greek word for birth and family.
intro.cn: gene 根据希腊语中表示出生和家族的词创造。

items.en: Genos meant birth, race, or family.
items.cn: genos 意为出生、种族或家族。

items.en: German scientists used Gen for a unit of heredity.
items.cn: 德国科学家用 Gen 表示遗传单位。

items.en: Johannsen coined gene in English in nineteen nine.
items.cn: 约翰森在一九〇九年用英语创造了 gene。

items.en: Genetics grew as the study of genes.
items.cn: 遗传学作为研究基因的学科发展起来。

items.en: The word also became a metaphor for built-in traits.
items.cn: 这个词也成为与生俱来特征的比喻。

note.en: Gene is compared with look-alike words and words from biology.
note.cn: 把 gene 与形近词以及生物学词汇作比较。

normalIntro.en: A gene is a small instruction that travels from one generation to the next.
normalIntro.cn: gene 是一条从一代传到下一代的小指令。

normal.en: Each gene carries a message.
normal.cn: 每个基因都携带一条信息。

normal.en: The gene for eye colour came from her mother.
normal.cn: 决定眼睛颜色的基因来自她母亲。

normal.en: Scientists studied a gene linked to the disease.
normal.cn: 科学家研究了一个与该疾病相关的基因。

normal.en: Gene therapy is still a young field.
normal.cn: 基因治疗仍是一个年轻的领域。

normal.en: The team has a gene for hard work.
normal.cn: 这支队伍有一种勤奋的内在因素。

abstract.en: A gene is a letter in a book no one has finished reading.
abstract.cn: 基因是一本还没人读完的书里的一个字母。

abstract.en: We inherit more than we can see.
abstract.cn: 我们继承的比能看见的更多。

abstract.en: Small instructions can shape a whole life.

sensesIntro.cn: gene 指遗传单位，或被认为决定某种特征的基本因素。

core.en: A small instruction passed down through life.
core.cn: 在生命间传递的小指令。

branches.en: A cell holds coded instructions.

definition_en: probable or expected; seeming suitable or promising; believable; and, as an adverb, probably
core_image: 云图上那片雨云正朝城市的方向缓缓压过来
scene: 清晨的广播里，播音员指着云图说今天午后有雨，出门的人顺手把伞塞进包里。 The forecaster said it was likely to rain by noon, so she took an umbrella.
sceneCN: 这里是「很可能的」（第 1 个义项：表示某事有较大机会发生）；句意为预报员说中午前很可能下雨，于是她带上了伞。图中可辨识物件：云图、铺开的雨云带、塞进包里的折叠伞。

senses.title: Probable or expected to happen
senses.titleCN: 很可能的；预期会发生的
senses.definition: having a high chance of happening or of being true
senses.definitionCN: 发生或属实的可能性很大
senses.example: It is likely to rain this evening.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚很可能下雨。
senses.why: The word grew out of like in the sense of having the same appearance, so something likely looks the way the expected thing looks, and that resemblance turns into probability.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从表示「长得像」的 like 长出来：一件很可能会发生的事，看起来正像预期中那件事的样子，于是「像」变成了「可能」。

senses.title: Seeming suitable or promising
senses.definition: seeming to be a good choice or to have a good chance of success
senses.definitionCN: 看起来是个好选择，或成功的机会很大
senses.example: She is the likeliest candidate for the post.
senses.exampleCN: 她是最有希望得到这个职位的人选。
senses.why: When a person looks the part, English calls that person likely, because the old sense of having the appearance of something turns into being promising.
senses.whyCN: 当一个人看起来就像那个角色，英语便说这人 likely，因为「具有某物的样子」这一旧义转成了「有希望」。

senses.title: Believable or plausible
senses.definition: seeming true or believable, often said of an excuse, an alibi or a story
senses.definitionCN: 听起来真实可信，常用于借口、不在场证明或说法
senses.example: That is a likely story, but I still do not believe it.
senses.exampleCN: 那说法倒像真的，可我还是不信。
senses.why: If something merely looks true, it can pass as true, and the ironic phrase a likely story shows exactly where appearance and credibility part company.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西只要看着像真的，就能冒充真的；反讽的「a likely story」正说明「像」与「可信」在哪儿分了家。

senses.title: Probably, as an adverb
senses.definition: used to say that something is probably true or will probably happen
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示某事大概属实或大概会发生
senses.example: They will likely agree to the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 他们大概会同意这个方案。
senses.why: The adjective ending -ly already carried the sense of manner, so the same form slid into adverb use without taking a second suffix.
senses.whyCN: 形容词词尾 -ly 本就带「以……方式」的意味，所以同一形式直接滑入副词用法，不必再加一个后缀。

intro.en: Likely began as a word for looking like something, and only later came to mean probable.
intro.cn: likely 最初表示「看起来像某物」，后来才引申为「很可能」。

items.en: A root reconstructed as līka- is generally thought to mean body or form, and from it came words for being similar in appearance.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个重构词根 līka-，意为「身体、形状」，由此产生表示「外观相似」的词。

items.en: Old English gelīc meant similar or alike, and the suffix -līc meant having the form of something.
items.cn: 古英语 gelīc 意为「相似的、相像的」，后缀 -līc 意为「具有……形状的」。

items.en: Old Norse líkligr, built from líkr and -ligr, meant likely or probable and strengthened the English word during the Norse period.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语 líkligr 由 líkr（相像）与 -ligr 构成，意为「可能的、像样的」，在诺尔斯语影响时期强化了英语中的这个词。

items.en: Middle English used likli and likely for both a probable event and a suitable person.
items.cn: 中古英语用 likli、likely 同时表示「可能发生的事」与「合适的人」。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adjective and adds a fully accepted adverb use, especially in American writing.
items.cn: 现代英语保留形容词，并发展出被广泛接受的副词用法，尤其在美式书面语中。

entries.definitionCN: 据现有证据推测大概如此。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on like, so every hook should connect appearance with probability.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在 like 之上，所以每条记忆钩子都该把「像」与「可能」连起来。

normal.en: Like and likely share a root: what looks like the expected thing is likely to become it.
normal.cn: like 与 likely 同根：看起来像预期结果的，很可能就会变成那个结果。

normal.en: The ending -ly marks manner and also builds adverbs, which is why likely serves as both adjective and adverb.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 既标记方式，又能构成副词，所以 likely 兼作形容词与副词。

normal.en: Unlikely is simply un- plus likely, and the stress stays on the first syllable of the base word.
normal.cn: unlikely 就是 un- 加 likely，重音仍落在原词的第一音节。

normal.en: Likelihood turns the adjective into a noun with -hood, the same ending seen in childhood and neighbourhood.
normal.cn: likelihood 用 -hood 把形容词变成名词，与 childhood、neighbourhood 用的是同一个后缀。

normal.en: A likely candidate looks the part, and a likely story sounds true; in both cases the eye or ear decides before the mind.
normal.cn: likely candidate 是「看着像那个人选」，a likely story 是「听着像真的」；两处都是眼睛或耳朵先于头脑作判断。

abstract.en: English first trusted the look of a thing, and then let that look become a guess about the future.
abstract.cn: 英语先相信一物的外观，再让这外观变成对未来的猜测。

abstract.en: Probability is appearance stretched over time: what resembles the usual outcome is expected to become it.
abstract.cn: 可能性就是把外观拉长时间：与常见结果相像的，就被预期会变成那个结果。

abstract.en: The same word serves a promise and a doubt, because a good appearance can raise either hope or suspicion.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能许诺也能怀疑，因为好看的外表既能让人起希望，也能让人起疑心。

examples.en: It is likely to rain this evening.
examples.cn: 今晚很可能下雨。

examples.en: She is the likeliest candidate for the post.
examples.cn: 她是最有希望得到这个职位的人选。

examples.en: They will likely agree to the plan.
examples.cn: 他们大概会同意这个方案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来客里」——来客里有人说这单生意能成，听着很可能；likely 就是很可能。

root: 一般认为源自重构词根 līka-（身体、形状），古英语有 gelīc（相似的）与后缀 -līc，古诺尔斯语 líkligr（可能的）进一步影响英语；与 like 同族，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is looking like something; from there the senses divide into probability, suitability, credibility, and the adverb use.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「看起来像某物」；义项由此分成概率、合适、可信三种判断，以及副词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a band of rain cloud slowly pressing toward the city on a weather map.
core.cn: 核心意象：云图上那片雨云正朝城市缓缓压过来。

branches.en: a cloud band crawling toward the city
branches.cn: 一条朝城市爬来的云带

branches.en: a name at the top of a shortlist
branches.cn: 候选名单最上面的一个名字

branches.en: an excuse that sounds almost true

branches.en: a forecast that shapes the morning
branches.cn: 左右了清晨安排的预报

intro.en: The word is held together by the Germanic root for form and the suffix that turned similarity into probability.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「形状」的日耳曼词根，以及把相似变成可能的那个后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 舒适；安逸；安慰；安慰（动词）
definition_en: a pleasant state of physical ease, kind words that make someone feel better, or to make someone feel less sad
core_image: 疲惫时陷进沙发里那口长长的叹气
scene: 她把热水袋塞进被窝，冰冷的双脚慢慢暖起来。 A warm blanket brought comfort on the cold night.
sceneCN: 这里 comfort 指「舒适；安逸」（第 1 个义项：身体上的安适）；句意是一条暖毯在寒夜里带来了舒适。

collocations.zh: 起不了多少作用的安慰

senses.title: A state of ease
senses.definition: a pleasant state in which you feel relaxed and free from pain
senses.definitionCN: 身体放松、没有痛楚的愉快状态
senses.example: The soft chair gave her back some comfort.
senses.exampleCN: 这把软椅让她的背舒服了一些。
senses.why: The first sense is about the body, since the old word meant to strengthen.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项关乎身体，因为这个词原意是使人变得强壮。

senses.title: Consolation
senses.definition: kind words or actions that make someone feel less sad
senses.definitionCN: 让人不那么难过的贴心话语或举动
senses.example: His letter was a great comfort to her.
senses.exampleCN: 他的来信给了她很大的安慰。
senses.why: Strength passes from one person to another, so comfort becomes solace.
senses.whyCN: 力量从一个人传到另一个人身上，舒适便成了安慰。

senses.title: To console
senses.definition: to make someone feel less sad or worried
senses.definitionCN: 使某人少一些悲伤或担忧
senses.example: She comforted the crying child.
senses.exampleCN: 她安慰着那个哭泣的孩子。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb: to give someone comfort.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：把舒适与安慰给出去。

intro.en: Comfort comes from Latin confortare, which meant to strengthen greatly.
intro.cn: comfort 来自拉丁语 confortare，本义是大大地增强力量。

items.en: Confortare joined com-, strongly, with fortis, meaning strong.
items.cn: confortare 把表示强化的 com- 与意为强壮的 fortis 结合。

items.en: The word was used for giving fresh strength to a tired person.
items.cn: 这个词用于给疲惫的人重新注入力量。

items.en: Old French conforter carried both help and encouragement.
items.cn: 古法语 conforter 兼有援助与鼓励之意。

items.en: English comfort first meant to strengthen or cheer.
items.cn: 英语 comfort 最初表示使强健或使振奋。

items.en: The sense of bodily ease and soft furnishings came later.
items.cn: 身体安适与柔软陈设的含义是后来才有的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs that share the opening of comfort, while the meaning group names ease and consolation.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 comfort 开头相同的动词，近义组列出安适与安慰。

entries.definition: to behave in a particular way
to face a problem or an opponent
to behave as others expect
the state of being free from pain or worry
entries.definitionCN: 没有痛苦或忧虑的状态

entries.definition: something that makes you feel better after loss
entries.definitionCN: 失去之后让人好受些的东西

entries.definition: to make a person or pain calmer

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a body at rest, then move to words that console and to the act of consoling.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从身体得到休息开始，再走到安慰的话语与安慰的动作。

normal.en: The Latin fortis means strong, so comfort is strength handed to someone.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 fortis 意为强壮，所以 comfort 是递给别人的力量。

normal.en: Soft chairs, warm blankets and hot drinks all deliver comfort.
normal.cn: 软椅、暖毯和热饮都在传递舒适。

normal.en: Cold comfort is a help that hardly helps at all.
normal.cn: 冷安慰是指几乎起不了作用的帮助。

normal.en: Your comfort zone is the place where nothing pushes you.
normal.cn: 舒适区就是没有东西推着你的那个地方。

normal.en: Comfort as a verb always takes a person as its object.
normal.cn: comfort 作动词时，宾语总是人。

abstract.en: Picture sinking into a sofa after a long bus ride.
abstract.cn: 想象长途汽车之后陷进沙发。

abstract.en: Picture a hand resting on a shaking shoulder.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手轻轻搭在颤抖的肩上。

abstract.en: Picture a warm drink placed silently on a cold desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯热饮被悄悄放在冰冷的桌上。

examples.en: The fire gave the small room a gentle comfort.
examples.cn: 炉火给这个小房间带来一种柔和的舒适。

examples.en: She comforted him with a few quiet words.
examples.cn: 她用几句轻声的话安慰了他。

examples.en: They now live in comfort by the sea.
examples.cn: 他们现在在海边过着安逸的生活。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 comfort 记成 com（一起）加 fort（堡垒）：一起躲进堡垒里，就有了舒适与安慰。

root: 源自拉丁语 confortare，com- 表强化，fortis 表强壮，本义是给人添力，后转为身体的安适与心里的安慰。

sensesIntro.en: From strength given to a tired body, to ease of body, then to consolation and the act of consoling.
sensesIntro.cn: 从给疲惫之躯添力，到身体的安适，再到安慰与安慰的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sinking into a sofa and letting out a long breath of relief.
core.cn: 核心意象：疲惫时陷进沙发里那口长长的叹气。

branches.en: Bodily ease is the sense most people meet first today.
branches.cn: 身体的安适是今天多数人最先接触到的义项。

branches.en: Consolation is ease given to a wounded heart.
branches.cn: 安慰是给受伤的心送去的安适。

branches.en: The verb is simply the act of handing comfort over.
branches.cn: 动词义就是把舒适递出去的动作。

branches.en: Soft things and kind words both answer the same tiredness.
branches.cn: 柔软的东西与温柔的话语回应的是同一种疲惫。

branches.en: One can comfort only by first noticing another's pain.
branches.cn: 只有先看见别人的痛，才谈得上安慰。

intro.en: Comfort is a free base that grows with -able, -ing and the negative prefix dis-.
intro.cn: comfort 是自由词基，靠 -able、-ing 与否定前缀 dis- 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Its Latin root fortis, strong, also hides inside fortress and fortify.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词根 fortis 意为强壮，也藏在 fortress 与 fortify 之中。

items.meaningCN: 没有温暖的；缺乏安慰的
items.example: The room felt cold and comfortless.

core_image: 前一步的脚印后面，紧接着下一个脚印

senses.why: This is the basic time sense.

senses.title: Only one

senses.why: This is the core sense of one alone.

senses.title: For one person

senses.title: Not married

senses.definitionCN: 未婚或没有固定伴侣的

senses.title: Power to give orders
senses.definition: the right or power to give orders and make decisions
senses.definitionCN: 下命令、作决定的资格或力量
senses.example: The manager has the authority to hire staff.
senses.exampleCN: 这位经理有权雇用员工。
senses.why: The Latin source auctor meant an originator, and the derived noun named the weight an originator carries, so authority is power that comes from standing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源 auctor 意为开创者，派生名词指开创者身上的分量，所以 authority 是由地位带来的权力。

senses.title: Official body
senses.definition: an official organization or government body with power in an area
senses.definitionCN: 在某领域拥有权力的官方组织或政府机构
senses.example: The local authority approved the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 地方当局批准了这项计划。
senses.why: Power is transferred from a person to an institution, so the plural authorities often means the people who run a city or a service.
senses.whyCN: 权力从个人转到机构身上，所以复数 authorities 常指管理一座城市或某项公共事务的部门。

senses.title: Trusted expert
senses.definition: a person whose knowledge or judgment is respected and trusted
senses.definitionCN: 知识或判断受人尊重与信任的人
senses.example: She is an authority on ancient coins.
senses.exampleCN: 她是古钱币方面的权威。
senses.why: Here the weight is intellectual rather than official: the person is trusted because of knowledge, not because of an office.
senses.whyCN: 这里的分量是知识上的而非官职上的：此人受信任靠的是学问，而不是职位。

intro.en: Authority names the weight that an originator carries.
intro.cn: authority 指开创者身上所带的分量。

items.en: auctor meant 'originator or promoter'.
items.cn: auctor 意为「开创者、推动者」。

items.en: auctoritas meant 'influence, weight or command'.
items.cn: auctoritas 意为「影响力、分量、号令」。

items.en: autorite carried the sense of rightful power.
items.cn: 古法语 autorite 带有「正当权力」的意思。

items.en: English authority covered power, office and expert opinion.
items.cn: 中古英语 authority 兼指权力、职位与专家意见。

items.en: The plural became the normal word for official bodies.
items.cn: 复数形式成为指官方机构的常用说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the auctor root; the near-meaning group gives words for power and expertise.
note.cn: 形近组共享 auctor 词根；近义组是表示权力与专业知识的词。

normalIntro.en: Authority is weight: official weight, institutional weight, or the weight of knowledge.
normalIntro.cn: authority 是一种分量：官职的分量、机构的分量，或知识的分量。

normal.en: The root is the same as in author: an originator carries weight.
normal.cn: 词根与 author 相同：开创者身上带着分量。

normal.en: The plural authorities usually means official bodies, not several powers.
normal.cn: 复数 authorities 通常指官方机构，而不是几种权力。

normal.en: An authority on a subject is a trusted expert.
normal.cn: an authority on a subject 指某领域可信的专家。

normal.en: The adjective authoritative keeps the -ative ending.
normal.cn: 形容词 authoritative 保留了 -ative 词尾。

normal.en: Do not confuse authority with author; one is weight, the other is a person.
normal.cn: 不要把 authority 与 author 混淆：一个是分量，一个是人。

abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章压在一张纸上。

abstract.en: See a raised hand that stops a whole room.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手抬起，整个房间都停下来。

abstract.en: See a thick reference book with a ribbon in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚厚的工具书，里面夹着书签带。

root: 源自拉丁语 auctoritas「影响力、号令」，来自 auctor「开创者」，词根 augere 意为「使生长」；经古法语 autorite 进入英语，由「开创者的分量」引申为权力、官方机构与专业权威。

sensesIntro.en: One word covers the right to command, the body that commands, and the expert who is trusted.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词涵盖下命令的资格、下命令的机构，以及受信任的专家。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an official stamp that makes a sheet of paper heavy.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚公章让一张纸变得有分量。

intro.en: The root auctor, 'originator', links authority with author and authorize.
intro.cn: 词根 auctor 意为「开创者」，把 authority 与 author、authorize 连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin augere, 'to increase', is the deeper root of the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 augere「增加」是整个词族更深的词源。

the state of being the author

definition_en: the legal ending of a marriage, or a complete separation between two things
core_image: 两只箱子原先把把手系在一起，绳结被剪断，各自拖开
scene: 门口两只旧箱子本来用绳系着，绳子已经剪断。 They agreed to a divorce after twenty years.
sceneCN: 这里 divorce 指「离婚」（第 1 个义项：依法结束婚姻）；句意是二十年后他们同意离婚。

senses.title: The legal end of a marriage
senses.definition: the official and legal ending of a marriage
senses.definitionCN: 婚姻在法律上正式结束
senses.example: The divorce was final in June.
senses.exampleCN: 离婚在六月正式生效。
senses.why: A shared life is untied by a document and a signature.
senses.whyCN: 共同的生活，被一纸文书和一枚签名解开。

senses.title: To end a marriage legally
senses.definition: to end your marriage with someone by law
senses.definitionCN: 依法结束与某人的婚姻
senses.example: She divorced him last year.
senses.exampleCN: 她去年和他离了婚。
senses.why: One person can begin the ending, even when both must sign.
senses.whyCN: 结束可以由一个人提出，却要两个人都签字。

senses.title: To cut two things apart
senses.definition: to separate two things that were closely joined
senses.definitionCN: 把原本紧密相连的两样东西分开
senses.example: You cannot divorce art from its time.
senses.exampleCN: 不能把艺术和它的时代分开。
senses.why: Some pairs only look joined, and part without a sound.
senses.whyCN: 有些搭配只是看着相连，分开时毫无声响。

intro.en: Divorce comes from Latin divortium, a turning apart, from divertere, to turn in different ways.
intro.cn: divorce 来自拉丁语 divortium（转开），源头是 divertere（转向不同方向）。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn, as a body turns away.
items.cn: vertere 指转动，像人转身那样。

items.en: Di- sent the two turning paths apart.
items.cn: 前缀 di- 把两条转向的路分开。

items.en: Divortium named the formal parting of a marriage.
items.cn: divortium 指婚姻的正式分离。

items.en: Old French divorce kept the legal sense.
items.cn: 古法语 divorce 保留了法律意味。

items.en: English used it for the ending of a marriage.
items.cn: 英语借入时指婚姻的结束。

items.en: Today ideas and habits can be divorced as well.
items.cn: 今天想法与习惯也可以用这个词分开。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the vertere turning, while the meaning group names other kinds of parting.
note.cn: 形近组保留 vertere 的「转」，近义组则是几种分开的名目。

entries.definition: to turn something aside
of many different kinds
a person whose marriage has ended
the state of living or being apart
entries.definitionCN: 生活上或位置上的分开

entries.definition: a break between two joined things
the end of a relationship

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with two cases tied by one rope and end with art cut off from its age.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从两只被一根绳系住的箱子开始，落到被割离时代的艺术。

normal.en: Di- plus vorce: the shared road turns into two roads.
normal.cn: di 加 vorce，共同的路转成两条。

normal.en: Their divorce was quiet and quickly arranged.
normal.cn: 他们的离婚安静而办得很快。

normal.en: She divorced him and moved to the coast.
normal.cn: 她和他离了婚，搬去了海边。

normal.en: You cannot divorce a song from the room it was sung in.
normal.cn: 不能把一首歌和它被唱的那个房间分开。

normal.en: A divorce from daily facts weakens any argument.
normal.cn: 脱离日常事实，任何论证都会变弱。

abstract.en: Picture two cases tied by a rope that is then cut.
abstract.cn: 想象两只箱子被一根绳系着，绳子随后被剪断。

abstract.en: Picture a page torn cleanly along a fold.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸沿着折痕整齐撕开。

abstract.en: Picture two names erased from one shared line.
abstract.cn: 想象两个名字从同一行里被擦掉。

examples.en: The divorce was final in June.
examples.cn: 离婚在六月正式生效。

examples.en: She divorced him after ten years.
examples.cn: 十年之后她和他离了婚。

examples.en: You cannot divorce art from its time.
examples.cn: 不能把艺术和它的时代分开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 divorce 记成「转开各自走」：di 表示分开，vorce 与转同源，原本并肩的两条路一转开，婚姻或关系也就断了。

root: 源自拉丁语 divortium，来自 divertere（转向不同方向），由 di-（分开）与 vertere（转）组成。本义是两人转身各走一边，专指婚姻在法律上结束，后来也用于把紧密相连的事物强行分开。

sensesIntro.en: From two cases cut loose from one rope to a piece of art torn from its own age.
sensesIntro.cn: 从两只被剪断绳子的箱子，到一件被割离自身时代的艺术品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two old cases tied by one rope, the knot cut, each dragged its own way.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只旧箱子被一根绳系着，绳结剪断，各自拖开。

branches.en: The first sense is the legal end as a fact.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是作为事实的法律结束。

branches.en: The second sense is the act of ending it.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是结束婚姻的那个动作。

branches.en: The third sense cuts apart things that are not marriages.
branches.cn: 第三个义项分开的不是婚姻。

branches.en: Both senses concern one marriage and two signatures.
branches.cn: 两个义项都关乎一桩婚姻与两个签名。

branches.en: Both senses describe a lasting separation.
branches.cn: 两个义项都描述一种持久的分开。

intro.en: Divorce belongs to the vertere family, where Latin vertere, to turn, also gives divert and diverse.
intro.cn: divorce 属于 vertere 一族，拉丁语 vertere（转）也给出 divert 与 diverse。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere, to turn, gives divorce and divert; di- turns one shared path into two.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere（转）给出 divorce 与 divert，前缀 di- 把一条共同的路变成两条。

items.meaning: a turning apart of two lives

items.example: He is divorced and lives alone.

items.exampleCN: 这位离异者搬到了国外。

items.example: The divorcement of the two ideas was complete.
items.exampleCN: 这两个想法彻底分开了。
